close_reason:
Verified independently: the README warning was stale. All five client queryChanges methods (Chat, Message, Space, ChatContact, CustomEmoji) have matching server handler registrations in crate-jmap-chat-server/src/lib.rs:166-274. Git log shows the handlers have existed since the chat-server's first commit (59ecc32). 5-for-5 match.

There is no actual client/server surface mismatch. The fix is removing the stale doc paragraph, not building a runtime helper or feature gate (options a / b in the bead) for a problem that doesn't exist. This is the 'might already be done' anti-pattern from workspace AGENTS.md.

Committed as 4ea7884.
description: README.md:248-250 documents: 'Some object types have queryChanges on the client without a corresponding handler in jmap-chat-server; check server capability before calling.' This is a known client/server contract gap. The client exposes methods that may produce server errors at runtime, with no compile-time gate, no feature flag, no runtime probe helper. Downstream callers have to read the README, remember to check capability themselves, and discover at runtime which methods are server-supported. Options: (a) add a runtime helper like has_query_changes(&self, type_name: &str) -> bool that consults Session capability advertisements; (b) feature-gate the unsupported methods; (c) accept the prose warning and live with the support tickets. The prose-only approach is the most honest in a kit-library posture (the consumer brings auth and policy), but a one-line helper would meaningfully reduce caller surprise.
title: queryChanges client/server surface mismatch is prose-only, no runtime helper
